llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed Beatra image-generation workflow, but it grants and retains broader Beatra account authority than its board-image purpose needs and silently self-updates executable package files.

dimensions.detail: Network access and user-selected file upload are proportionate to a paid remote image service, while full-scope shared account credentials and arbitrary remote tool routing are broader than the stated board-still use case.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package documents its Beatra device-authorization flow, browser approval, private credential storage, and uninstall process; these are disclosed, but they create sensitive local account state under ~/.beatra.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The Skill instructions require user approval before paid image generation and constrain the normal workflow, but the bundled MCP client exposes a generic call path for any remote tool name without a package-side allowlist.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill stores a reusable shared bearer token and local inventory/update state, and its client silently checks for and installs package updates by default, replacing package-owned scripts and instructions without separate confirmation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The board-pack workflow is coherent with remote image generation, task polling, optional reference upload, and billing reads, but the authorization scope also covers unrelated video, music, speech, voice write, broad wallet spending, artifact reads, and task cancellation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if you are not comfortable giving Beatra a persistent shared device token with broad media, wallet, artifact, and task permissions. Disable automatic updates with the documented update command if you require reviewed code to remain unchanged, and only run paid generation after checking the live credit card and approval prompt.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The uninstall and disconnect behavior is a disclosed lifecycle workflow and is user-initiated, with safeguards to avoid revoking a shared Beatra connection while other skills remain; this finding is downgraded as a standalone concern.
[AE1] unexpected: The referenced bundled client was locally present and inspectable in this workspace, so the scanner's partial-inspection concern was not supported as analysis evasion for this adjudication.
[SDI-4] expected: Balance, ledger, and top-up messaging are coherent for a paid remote generation service and are disclosed in the Skill, though the public summary does not strongly foreground account-credit handling.
[PE3] expected: Credential use is expected for the authenticated Beatra MCP service and the code applies private-file handling, but the credential is shared and broad-scoped, which contributes to the Review verdict.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The broad OAuth scope set and generic MCP client exceed the image-board workflow, especially for non-image media and voice capabilities.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Silent default self-update of scripts and Skill instructions is disclosed but not necessary for the board-image purpose and materially changes post-review behavior.
[RA1] unexpected: The exposed update command and default automatic update path allow package self-modification; this is better treated as Review risk than evidence of current malicious code.
[T05] unexpected: The static finding is supported by artifact evidence: authorization requests unrelated capabilities and the client forwards arbitrary tool names to the MCP endpoint.
[T03] unexpected: The static finding is supported in part: the updater uses fixed HTTPS endpoints, checksums, path checks, rollback, and an off switch, but it still silently retrieves and replaces executable package content by default without independent release signatures visible in the artifact.
